_note: What is on the discs, entered by hand from the High-Def Digest and dvdmg.com reviews, and from tvacdb.sandboxen.com for the commentaries. Runtimes are the reviewers' stopwatch figures where they gave one. Each becomes its own entry in the week its set came out; build/data/additions.json is generated from this. `k` is the column the extra belongs in: `bts` for making-of material, `evo` for footage and artefacts that are part of the fiction rather than about it. `src` on a set is where the blurbs came from.

s1.b: Cut material from nineteen of the twenty-three episodes. Mostly extensions rather than lost plot -- the exception is Genesis, whose trims belong to the terrorist thread the series dropped.
The short official overview: where the idea came from, how the cast was found, the Comic-Con debut that made it a phenomenon before it aired.
The difference between an effect done on set and one done in a computer, worked through on the scene where Hiro stops time in a Tokyo street.
Stunt coordinator Ian Quinn on how the falls and fights were staged, with raw on-set footage of the takes.

s1.t: A Profile of Artist Tim Sale
s1.b: The comics artist who painted everything Isaac Mendez paints, on his career and on working colour-blind.
Wendy Melvoin and Lisa Coleman on writing and recording the series' music.
A numerical parlour trick on disc five, dressed up as a test of Matt Parkman's telepathy.

s1ce.t: Cast at the Museum of Television and Radio
s1ce.b: A bonus disc unique to the Collector's Edition: three quarters of an hour of the cast and crew in conversation at the Museum of Television and Radio, sold nowhere else.
Not a feature but four objects in the box: miniature reproductions of Isaac Mendez's prophetic canvases, painted for the series by Tim Sale.

s2.t: Heroes Season Two: A New Beginning
s2.b: A promotional overview of the new season and its new characters, made to be watched before the episodes rather than after.
Allan Arkush and Greg Beeman take a few scenes apart and explain what it took to shoot each one.
Cast and crew promising the next year will be extraordinary, with almost no detail attached.
Trims from six episodes -- an alternate opening for Nathan, more of Hiro in feudal Japan, more of Monica in New Orleans.
The finale as it was first cut, reusing much of the aired footage but sending the virus somewhere very different.

s2.t: Behind the Alternate Ending of Generations
s2.b: Tim Kring, Jeph Loeb and Jesse Alexander on why the ending changed -- the one place on any of these discs where the writers' strike is discussed directly.
Scenes shot for the twelfth and thirteenth episodes of a season that stopped at eleven. Mostly Elle hunting Sylar.
Three web teasers made to look like camera-phone footage: Hotel Corinthian Explosion, Maya y Alejandro Viral Video, and Nathan and Peter Brooklyn Cam.

s2.t: Tim Sale Gallery of Screen Art
s2.b: Close-ups of the paintings Sale made for the series.

s3.b: Includes the Hard Knox webisodes, cut in among the trims rather than listed as a series of their own.
Stunt coordinator Tim Gilbert on staging the abilities, with before-effects footage of how the shots actually looked on set.
The effects team on turning those plates into finished shots, including the ruined-future sequence.
A mock advertisement for the company's civilian front.
A walk through the show's gold room, where the props worth keeping ended up -- including Isaac's original canvases.
Four segments on specific shots: Claire's brain, the deformed test subject's prosthetics, Daphne's speed, and the Matt-and-Danko chase.
Tim Kring, Adam Armus and Aron Eli Coleite on what they were trying to do with the Villains and Fugitives volumes.

s3.t: Tim Sale Gallery of Screen Art
s3.b: The season's paintings, including the ones painted onto rock.

s4.b: Trims across the season, spread over all four discs.
Zachary Quinto, Tim Kring and Adam Armus on the character the series could never quite finish with.
How the comics, the webisodes and the online campaign were meant to fit around the show.
Milo Ventimiglia on comics, and on the ones he was publishing himself.
The longest of these: several sequences taken apart shot by shot, including the car filling with water.
Recorded after the cancellation and hidden before the last episode, saying the story was not finished.

hr.b: Trims from nine of the thirteen episodes.
Tim Kring and the cast, old and new, on returning to the story five years after it ended.

s1.eps: the unaired pilot (Tim Kring alone), Godsend, The Fix, Distractions, Run!, Unexpected, Company Man, Parasite, .07%, Five Years Gone, The Hard Part, Landslide and How to Stop an Exploding Man

s2.eps: all eleven episodes, from Four Months Later... to Powerless

s3.eps: all twenty-five episodes of Villains and Fugitives

s4.eps: Once Upon a Time in Texas, Shadowboxing, The Fifth Stage and Brave New World

not_entries: Season 2: Takezo Kensei: Sword Saint -- not a disc release. yamagatofellowship.org began airing the five-part documentary on 27 August 2007; the timeline lists it there, under Evolutions, and the panel says the discs also carry it.
Season 2: Global News Interactive / The Drucker Files -- not a disc release either. Hana Gitelman posted the four clips to her blog on 13 December 2007; that is where the timeline lists it.
Season 3: Alternate Stories: The Recruit / Going Postal / Nowhere Man -- these are the webisodes, already listed in the week each went out. The discs collect them, which the panel says.
Season 4: Heroes Connections -- disc navigation art, not a feature.
corrections: Gabriel's list gave 18 min for Behind the Alternate Ending of Generations; that is the runtime of the alternate ending itself. The discussion after it runs about 11.
Season one's Special Effects is 10 min on High-Def Digest and 8:44 on dvdmg; the shorter figure is the one with a stopwatch behind it.
Season four's Deconstructing Sylar and Heroes Revolution are 20:43 and 10:45, close enough to the 20 and 10 given.
